text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 — Elevated DNS resolution latency for eu-west-2 observed by healthchecks (dns-resolver-probe)
ops-engineer-maria: seeing a big uptick in DNS timeouts from our eu edge -> led to upstream 502s in model-serving. graph: ~20-40% queries > 1s.
netops-jon: confirmed. Cloudflare resolver telemetry shows increased SERVFAILs from 2a availability zone and Route53 health checks show probe divergence. Possible propagation/TTL thrash.
sre-priya: assigning on-call. I'm inbound to bridge. Can you paste the current dig output?
ops-engineer-maria: piling a quick sample:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.eu
192.0.2.10
192.0.2.11
;; Query time: 1204 msec
;; SERVER: 1.1.1.1#53(1.1.1.1)
```
netops-jon: also seeing mixed answers from Route53 NS in different regions: eu-west-2 NS returning old weights for some clients. TTLs set at 60s but some resolvers caching longer.
platform-elena: any recent Route53 changes or deploys to GeoDNS config? I didn't touch it. No rollout in last 24h.
ops-engineer-maria: looks external — maybe Cloudflare broke a subset of resolvers, causing fallback to stale records and resulting traffic loops to non-optimal AZs.
sre-priya: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) reduce primary region weight so we failover traffic to eu-west-1 as controlled 2) increase TTL temporarily to stop oscillation? 3) add a short-term DNS answer that points to standby ALB in eu-west-1. Thoughts?
netops-jon: I can push a weighted-change to Route53 (change weight primary->50, standby->50) but that increases traffic on standby. Need owner approval.
sre-priya: do it, but throttle rate to avoid overloading standby. Also open a Cloudflare ticket: their resolvers showing 5xx/servfail. @support-ravi please raise with cloudflare SOC and attach probe logs.
support-ravi: on it. Creating ticket now and tagging escalation. Ticket ID CF-2026-839.
ops-engineer-maria: applying temporary Route53 weight change now: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://weights.json`
ops-engineer-maria: weights.json used: `{ "Changes": [{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.eu.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-2","Weight":50,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"192.0.2.10"}] } , {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.eu.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":50,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"198.51.100.5"}]}}]}`
incident-bot: Change submitted. ChangeInfo ID: /change/CZ987654321. Status: PENDING
netops-jon: after change, resolver mix looks more even, but Cloudflare still rates some queries causing SERVFAIL. I'm going to add a Route53 failover record for a static standby hostname as well.
platform-elena: also recommend enabling short-term DNS caching on our edge (prefix caching) to reduce query volume while providers stabilize. Priya, can we toggle prefix cache in runtime?
sre-priya: yes, enabling prefix caching knob now. `curl -XPOST https://console.api.internal/flags -d '{"prefix_cache_ttl": 120}'` — done.
ops-engineer-maria: monitoring: 502s dropped from 18% -> 7% in last 6 minutes. DNS latency still high for ~10% of clients.
support-ravi: bumped priority with Cloudflare: they say they're investigating partially degraded resolver in eu region; provided dig samples and timestamps.
netops-jon: added failover A records to point some queries to standby ALB `api-standby-eu-west-1.redwood` with TTL 30. Change propagation looks fine from public checks.
sre-priya: preparing customer communication: impact - some EU customers saw transient failed requests and elevated latency between 10:18 and ongoing. Estimated affected requests ~6% of global p95 traffic, mostly originating from EU resolvers using CF cluster X. Draft msg for external status?
support-ravi: draft: "We are investigating elevated DNS resolution latency affecting a subset of EU customers. We're applying DNS routing updates and failover to reduce impact. Root cause being investigated with Cloudflare and Route53. No data loss."
platform-elena: LGTM. Add ETA for next update in 30 minutes and link to postmortem when available.
ops-engineer-maria: on-call handoff in 45 min; Priya will take next shift. Priya, take point for post-incident next-steps.
sre-priya: taking handoff. I'll keep bridge for at least an hour and start a follow-up task: identify why Cloudflare resolvers returned inconsistent caches and whether our health checks or TTLs need tuning.
incident-bot: :page_with_curl: Incident created: INC-2026-1123, severity=SEV2, owner=sre-priya, bridge=https://meet.internal/INC-2026-1123
ops-engineer-maria: adding retrospective action items now: - investigate probe coverage gaps - consider raising Route53 TTL floor to 120s for geo records - add automated weight-smoothing to prevent oscillation
support-ravi: CS notified for high-touch customers listed in pgp/team. No immediate escalations from customer PMs.
netops-jon: Cloudflare replied: rolling mitigation on their resolver fleet in eu cluster, monitoring for 15 min.
sre-priya: monitoring metrics show recovery trend. Keeping incident open while Cloudflare confirms stable. If we see reversion, we'll trigger rollback of weight change.
platform-elena: good job triaging. We'll document configuration changes and timeline in the postmortem.
ops-engineer-maria: final note before handoff: keep DNS debug trace `dig +trace` samples and attach to incident. Saved to /var/logs/incidents/1767000000/dig-traces.log
sre-priya: handoff accepted. I'll update `last_message_ts` when we resolve. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
